text:
Maria Chen: Heads-up — error budget dashboard spiked negative during the US-west network blip last night. Burn rate went < 0 for ~20m. Panel: https://grafana/redwood/d/EB/errbud?panel=3

Sam Ortiz: I pulled the scrape logs. Prometheus had gaps for `requests_total` in us-west during the outage. rate()/increase() dropped to 0 and the derived ratio produced a negative-looking burn when we subtract from baseline.

Jen Park: Our current SLO query is basically:
```
(1 - (sum(increase(errors_total[5m])) / sum(increase(requests_total[5m]))))
```
When `requests_total` is missing, `increase()` returns 0 which flips the math.

Kai Li: Two quick mitigations: handle staleness and smooth the signal. For staleness, use a denominator fallback or `clamp_min`. Example:
```
sum(increase(errors_total[5m]))
/
clamp_min(sum(increase(requests_total[5m])), 1)
```
Or precompute a recording rule so Grafana/alerts use the same series.

Jen Park: Strongly +1 for a recording rule: `slo_requests_5m = sum(increase(requests_total[5m]))` and same for errors. That avoids small query drift across panels.

Sam Ortiz: Also add `for: 10m` on the SLO alert to avoid paging on short scrape gaps. And consider `avg_over_time` or increasing the window to 10m for the burn rate calc to reduce noise.

infra-bot: Deploy log: updated alerting ruleset `slo-alerts-v3` (deployer=infra-pipeline) — added clamp_min on denom and `for: 10m`.

Maria Chen: Another vector: cross-region rollup. us-west gaps made the global rollup look invalid because some regions returned NaN/0 and the rollup formula didn't weight by traffic.

Kai Li: For global rollup do a weighted average by requests: e.g.
```
sum(region) (err_rate_region * requests_region) / sum(region) (requests_region)
```
Ensure `requests_region` is `or vector(0)` or uses `clamp_min` so missing regions don't divide oddly.

Jen Park: We should also export `sample_count` and `scrape_coverage_percent` with the EB export so consumers can ignore low-confidence windows.

Sam Ortiz: I'll open a PR to the exporter to add `sample_count` and `scrape_coverage_percent` labels/metrics.

Maria Chen: TL;DR action items:
- Jen: add recording rules for requests/errors 5m.
- Sam: update alert queries to use clamp_min/fallback, increase window, add sample_count to EB exporter (PR incoming).
- Kai: change dashboard rollup to weighted avg and add runbook note.
- Maria: update runbook language about interpreting negative burn as "insufficient metric coverage" rather than a true credit.

Kai Li: I'll add the runbook note now.

Jen Park: I'll draft the recording-rule PR today and link it here.

Sam Ortiz: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/observability/pull/842 — includes clamp_min and `for: 10m` change. Needs review.

Maria Chen: Thanks everyone. If we can get the fixes merged before next on-call rotation that would reduce false positives a lot. :thumbsup:
